signals.title: AUD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Geopolitical Shock
signals.text: The G10 Currency Strength Scorecard registers JPY as the strongest currency (+1.877% 1-week average across 7 pairs) while AUD is the weakest (-2.708% 1-week average across 4 pairs), producing a 4.585% spread that triggers a critical bilateral theme. AUD/JPY trades at 104.922, well below its SMA20 of 107.50 and SMA50 of 108.10. While RBA 4.85% vs BoJ 1.25% provides a +360bp OIS carry advantage to AUD, the market is aggressively unwinding carry positions due to severe risk aversion. VIX has surged 26.20% to 35.9, reflecting extreme equity market stress, while maritime mine strikes near the Strait of Hormuz layer acute geopolitical risk. Furthermore, AUD positioning shows a late-trend exhaustion with COT LF net long collapsing WoW by -15,052 contracts to +26,143 (pctl 19), while retail traders are 91% long, creating extreme contrarian risk. Trade bias: Bearish AUD/JPY; risk-off liquidation overrides carry advantage. Catalyst: Japan Services PMI at 00:30 UTC. Risk: VIX retracing below 25 or swift de-escalation in Middle East shipping corridors.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry vs Options Skew + Volatility Premium
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 158.597, holding between its SMA50 at 157.95 and SMA200 at 158.85. The Fed 4.00% vs BoJ 1.25% policy rate differential maintains a +275bp nominal advantage (+268bp via OIS SOFR vs TONA), anchoring structural support. However, the options market is pricing sharp downside risk: 25d Risk Reversals sit at -1.77, indicating strong put skew and heavy hedging against a drop toward 155.00. 1M ATM Implied Volatility runs at 7.5% against 30-day Realized Volatility of 5.7%, yielding a +1.8% Volatility Risk Premium that signals option market fear. JPY COT LF net short stands at -29,545 contracts (pctl 85, z +1.12), showing crowded spec short exposure vulnerable to unwinding if risk asset liquidation accelerates. Trade bias: Neutral/Bearish USD/JPY, downside option hedging competes with structural carry. Catalyst: US 2-Year Note Auction at 18:00 UTC. Risk: US 10Y yield rising back toward 5.00% to reinforce carry bid.

signals.title: USD/CAD — COT vs Options Skew Divergence + Retail Extreme
signals.text: USD/CAD trades at 1.4341, remaining in a strong technical uptrend above its SMA20 (1.4140) and SMA50 (1.4131). The Fed 4.00% vs BoC 2.50% rate differential offers a +150bp carry advantage (+136bp via OIS) favoring the greenback. COT LF net positioning on CAD is heavily short at -75,447 contracts (pctl 37), but specs added +17,342 net longs over the 4-week window despite WoW shorts accumulating by -5,235. In contrast, 25d Risk Reversals sit near neutral at +0.19, showing options markets are refusing to pay up for upside USD/CAD calls despite spot breaking higher. This institutional options divergence is compounded by extreme retail positioning, where Retail sentiment data shows retail traders are 92% short (8% long), creating massive squeeze potential if spot extends above 1.4400. Trade bias: Bullish USD/CAD; retail extreme short squeezed by carry and commodity weakness. Catalyst: US Consumer Confidence at 15:00 UTC. Risk: Bank of Canada hawkish pivot or sharp rebound in WTI crude above $88/bbl.

signals.title: GBP/USD — ESI Support vs Technical Downtrend
signals.text: GBP/USD trades at 1.3099, failing to reclaim its SMA20/50 cluster at 1.3304/1.3302 and remaining anchored in a technical downtrend below the SMA200 at 1.3400. The BoE 4.00% policy rate vs Fed 4.00% yields a 0bp nominal spread, though OIS SONIA vs SOFR gives GBP a minor +7bp carry edge. Macro data remains supportive, with the UK Economic Surprise Index at +9.5 (moderate positive bias) compared to weaker global peers. COT LF net positioning remains net long at +23,730 contracts (pctl 38), though specs trimmed longs significantly with a WoW delta of -11,856 contracts. 25d Risk Reversals show a mild put skew of -0.61, indicating orderly demand for downside protection rather than panic. Trade bias: Bearish GBP/USD; technical breakdown below moving average cluster dominates positive data surprises. Catalyst: UK S&P Global Flash PMIs at 09:30 UTC. Risk: Flash PMIs beat consensus expectations significantly to trigger technical short covering above 1.3200.
